note: Hand-adjudicated gold labels for the evidence matrix. THIS FILE HOLDS 4 ARTIFACTS AND 42 CELLS. Every cell below was read out of the real corpus document named by doc_id and carries the reason in `note`. Cells nobody adjudicated are simply not here: an absent row is NOT an `unobserved` agreement, it is excluded from every denominator (see label_eval.ts). A verdict records what the ARTIFACT shows, never what the product is known to do elsewhere: `absent` means the place this feature would have appeared was inspected in this document and was empty; `unobserved` means the document is silent and silence carries no signal.

cells.note: "In the product you can create projects to collaborate with your team members"; work packages live inside projects and projects have members.
A whole "Manage members" section: "How to add existing members or invite new members to a project."
"Add members — How to add existing members or invite new members to a project"; the members filter lists "Invited — returns all users that have been invited, but have not yet registered".
"A role is defined as a set of permissions defined by a unique name. Project members are assigned to a project by specifying a user's ... name and the role(s) they should assume."
"You can check this setting in the Roles and Permissions section of the system administration" — roles and their permissions are configured by an administrator, not fixed.
Work packages are shared per record with a per-share role: "Work package shares provides filters based on all the roles available for sharing work packages ... View / Comment / Edit".
"A work package ... may have various additional attributes, such as status, assignee, priority, due date."
"Work package relations and hierarchies — How to create work package relations and hierarchies."
"you will be notified about important changes that are relevant to you, whether they are new comments that mention you"; clicking a notification "will open the Activity tab of this work package".
"a red badge on the notification bell icon ... The number on the badge indicates the number of total unread notifications", plus "Mark notifications as read" — an in-app centre with a read state.
The actors/permissions material was inspected and directly contradicts single-user use: "You must be a member of a project to view and work in it", members, groups, roles, administrators.

The document enumerates the views it has — "table view, split screen view, details view" — and no board/kanban is among them. The list is the declared place this would appear and it is empty. (This is a claim about THIS document, not about the product.)
"It is typically used to charge customers in eCommerce Shopping Cart type flows" — money is collected through the app's own payment APIs.
"to add a payment method corresponding to Stripe via a token, the Stripe plugin expects a field named `token`"; gateway plugins (Adyen, PayPal) are the whole subject.
"the product (the product Admin UI) to handle refunds, chargebacks, adjustments" plus a "#### Refund" direct-payment API that goes through the gateway plugin.
"the product core billing engine to charge for subscriptions"; the default payment method "is assumed to be used for recurring payments".
"designed to offer a single payment API for any type of payment gateway" — the document IS the customer-facing API reference.
Named third parties throughout: "Adyen notifications, Recurly push notifications, PayPal or BitPay IPN", Stripe, PayU Latam.
The payment configuration surface is described in detail (plugin registration, plugin properties, credentials, demos) and no sandbox or test mode appears anywhere in it.
Currency is never discussed. The only money figure is "given an order of $10" in an example. Silence, not a negative — do not read single-currency into it.
"Multi-tenancy: Each channel can be configured with its own set of products, shipping methods, payment methods, etc. This allows you to run multiple shops from a single the product server."
"Roles are the foundation of the product's role-based access control (RBAC) system. A Role is a named collection of Permissions."
"Beyond the built-in roles, administrators can create any number of custom roles ... defined by selecting the specific permissions it should grant."
"we also specify a 'platform fee' percentage, which is the percentage of the total Order value which the marketplace will collect as a fee. The remaining amount is then split between the Sellers."
"the marketplace may collect all payments and then later disburse the funds to the Sellers"; each Seller carries a `connectedAccountId`.
Prices are per channel and each channel is a seller's shop: "If an administrator of the UK channel changes the USD price to $20, the price in the Default channel will remain at $30."
"there is a one-to-many relation from `ProductVariant` to `ProductVariantPrice`"; ProductVariant is a first-class catalog entity.
"Each Channel has a set of `availableCurrencyCodes` ... you are able to define multiple prices in different currencies on a single product variant."

Seller onboarding is described step by step and has no approval gate: "a new mutation in the Shop API which allows a new seller to register", whose listed effects create the Seller, Channel, Role, ShippingMethod and StockLocation immediately.

The same onboarding walkthrough ends "Bob can now log in to the Dashboard ... and begin creating products to sell!" — no review step before a listing is live, in a document that does describe the order state machine in detail.
Reviews, ratings and reputation are never mentioned in this guide at all. Nothing was inspected, so this is a missing observation, not a negative.
What is booked is a provider's time: "Go to Users → Providers, select the provider, and adjust their working plan."
Each provider has their own working plan with breaks: "the default working plan includes breaks that don't leave enough room for your service ... adjust their working plan."
"the product can sync appointments with Google Calendar in both directions. When a provider links their Google Calendar, any changes made in either system will be reflected in the other."
"Google Calendar synchronization" in the feature list, plus a whole CalDAV (Baikal) sync guide.
"Email notification system" in the feature list.
"Multi-language interface" in the feature list.
"Log in to the product backend and go to the Calendar page"; providers are users under Users → Providers.
The document repeatedly describes a backend people log in to and a Users section with providers, so the actors material was inspected and is not single-user-no-login.
The notification capability is enumerated in the feature list as "Email notification system" and nothing else; SMS appears nowhere in the guide.
Same enumerated feature list: email only. Reminders by SMS are not offered anywhere in the document.
Money, payments, deposits and fees are never mentioned in this README/FAQ/sync guide. Silence — do not record a negative for a subject the document never opens.
